title: 2,500 Merges A Day. Then 30,000.
caption:
My bottleneck has never once been typing the code.

Anthropic's monorepo went from about 2,500 merges a day in May to over 30,000 in September, and git stopped keeping up. Almost 100 GB of main-branch history. On the order of 25 million CI checkouts a day. Several hundred git mirrors that outgrew their own disks. So they left git and migrated the whole monorepo to something they built themselves, in five months, with seven people.

The part I keep thinking about: Claude wrote most of the replacement for the problem Claude caused, and the engineers said their actual job was telling it no — steering it off over-engineering for hypothetical concerns. They're not releasing it either. They say it only makes sense if you have tens of thousands of engineers or swarms of agents.

I'm nowhere near that scale and my CI is still the slowest thing I own. What's your bottleneck?
